Generally speaking, refusing to move out is not advisable and could actually put you at greater risk than the dispute itself. While your landlord shouldn't be able to keep money that belongs to you, withholding possession of the property can give them grounds for an unlawful detainer action—meaning they might sue for immediate eviction rather than just fighting over the deposit amount.

The specific rules vary significantly by location. Some jurisdictions require landlords to return deposits within a set timeframe after vacancy with itemized deductions; others allow "withholding" until repairs are made if damage exceeds normal wear-and-tear. A few places even mandate interest payments on held deposits. Without knowing where this happened or what your lease says about notice periods and move-out conditions, I cannot tell you which path applies to you.

Instead of holding out, consider: documenting any damages (photos/video), requesting written accounting in writing, checking local tenant rights resources for your city/county, and potentially filing a claim in small claims court *after* moving out rather than delaying the process yourself. If there's significant money involved or safety concerns, consulting a local tenant advocacy group would be more useful than either side escalating unilaterally.
